project.name: algebraic-groups
project.description: Reusable Lean formalization of matrix point groups, finite algebraic group schemes and their coordinate algebras. The library covers unitriangular and upper-triangular groups, diagonal products, split kernels, closed unitriangular stages and their underlying affine-space presentations, finite additive products and positive-stage underlying projections and sections, unitriangular scalar base change and coherence, and selected dimension and geometric results. Coalgebra APIs include field subcoalgebras and finite-dimensional containment, right comodules and finitely generated subcomodule containment, coefficient matrix units, counit ranges and idempotent principal ideal constructors; split free presentations give finite tensor coordinates. Precise hypotheses and exclusions are documented in README.md and the focused mathematical guides. This is not a complete formalization of any cited source.

scope: This repository contains reusable algebraic-group, group-scheme and coordinate-algebra definitions and results, with focused ordinary-import clients. Every finite subset of a coalgebra over a commutative semiring with projective ambient module lies in a module-finitely-generated submodule with every-member first-factor tensor-image closure, without ambient finite generation. Free modules are included. Over a field, finite subsets have two-factor tensor-image containment. The restricted coalgebra structures over a field are provided by the subcoalgebra API. Finite biorthogonal ambient coordinates give coefficient-comultiplication and counit laws. Finite Hopf coefficient matrices satisfying both matrix laws are units with entrywise antipode inverse, including empty indices. For every coalgebra over a commutative semiring, the counit range is an idempotent ideal acting on the top submodule with image top. Idempotent principal ideals have explicit coalgebra constructors, including nonfree examples. Arbitrary split free presentations give finite tensor reconstruction and all-index contraction formulas without assuming freeness or finite generation of the presented module. Unitriangular point groups have central, lower-central and derived series, superdiagonal quotient and exponent results with the hypotheses described in their guides. Closed superdiagonal stages have Hopf coordinate quotients, multiplicative points, a polynomial-algebra presentation and underlying over-scheme affine-space isomorphisms over arbitrary commutative bases. These stages are normal; positive stages have primitive group-scheme coordinate projections whose successor is their underlying over-scheme kernel; the positive-stage projection has a specified underlying over-scheme section, without a quotient or a group-scheme splitting claim. The literal finite product of additive group schemes has underlying polynomial affine space over arbitrary commutative rings, preserving actual projections (including empty indices and zero rings). Diagonal, triangular, GL and SL constructions include selected products, representations, finite geometry and dimension results. Unitriangular coordinate algebras and group schemes have base-change and identity/tower coherence comparisons. Over a field, subcoalgebras are subspaces whose members' comultiplication lies in the image of their tensor square. Their subtypes carry the restricted coalgebra, with bundled inclusions and unique codomain restriction for homomorphisms. Every finitely generated subspace, and every finite subset, lies in a finite-dimensional subcoalgebra. No finite-dimensional ambient module or algebra structure is required, and no least finite closure is asserted. For a central bialgebra map from a commutative bialgebra A over a commutative ring R to a possibly noncommutative Hopf algebra B, the tensor-quotient equivalence compares B tensor_A B with B tensor_R (B / (ker counit_A)B) as first-factor B-modules. In this generality the target uses only the original module quotient, and A need not have an antipode. When B is commutative, tensorQuotientAlgEquiv refines the same map to a B-algebra equivalence on the canonical tensor and quotient algebras. Its simp toLinearEquiv equality recovers tensorQuotientEquiv and its finite-comultiplication formulas in both directions. Mixed scalar extension is a composition of tensor cancellation and congruence for compatible ordinary algebra maps and scalar towers, with no Hopf structure required on the commutative coefficient algebra. The library is not a blanket arbitrary-base classification or full quotient-effectivity theory, or complete formalization of Milne's book. Read exact limitations with each mathematical guide.

highlights.title: Closed linear embeddings of affine algebraic groups
highlights.statement: Every affine group scheme locally of finite type over a field K admits a group-scheme morphism into GL_n over K for some natural number n whose underlying scheme morphism is a closed immersion. Nonreduced group schemes are included, with no representation or basis supplied.

highlights.title: Point representations and comodules
highlights.statement: For a commutative Hopf algebra over a commutative ring and a fixed arbitrary module, natural point representations on the module's scalar extensions, tested on commutative base algebras in any universe containing the Hopf algebra, correspond bijectively to right-comodule structures on that module.

highlights.title: Finite-dimensional subcoalgebra containment
highlights.statement: Every finite subset of a coalgebra over a field is contained in a finite-dimensional subcoalgebra.

highlights.title: Finite Hopf algebras and right Hopf modules
highlights.statement: Every finite-dimensional Hopf algebra H over a field K admits a K-linear functional λ whose multiplication pairing (a, x) ↦ λ(a * x) is nondegenerate in both arguments. The Hopf algebra need not be commutative or cocommutative, and no restriction on the characteristic or assumption of antipode bijectivity is required. Over a commutative semiring, a specified right comodule over a possibly noncommutative semiring Hopf algebra with a given compatible right action and scalar tower is linearly equivalent to its coinvariants tensored with that Hopf algebra, without flatness or finiteness assumptions.

highlights.title: Bidual coactions and the antipode square
highlights.statement: For a specified right comodule on a finite projective module over a commutative semiring, canonical bidual evaluation identifies its bidual with the original coaction twisted on coefficients by the antipode square. The coefficient Hopf algebra need not be commutative and its antipode need not be invertible. For commutative coefficients the twist is identity.

headlines.title: Cartier's theorem
headlines.text:
Every commutative Hopf algebra over a characteristic-zero
field is reduced, and is smooth if it is finite type, for its given coefficient algebra
structure and with independent scalar and carrier universes. See
[Hopf algebra smoothness](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/algebraic-groups/blob/cad2dc41da14fb003738f0a032601dfa4d203453/AlgebraicGroups/Algebra/HopfAlgebra/Smooth.lean).

headlines.title: Linear embeddings of affine algebraic groups
headlines.text:
Every affine group scheme
locally of finite type over a field `K` admits a group-scheme morphism
`G → GLₙ` for some `n : ℕ` whose underlying scheme morphism is a closed
immersion. No basis or representation is supplied, and nonreduced group
schemes are included.
See the [closed linear embedding theorem](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/algebraic-groups/blob/cad2dc41da14fb003738f0a032601dfa4d203453/AlgebraicGroups/GroupScheme/ComoduleGeneralLinear.lean).

headlines.title: Surjectivity and faithfully flat coordinates
headlines.text:
For homomorphisms of
given affine group schemes locally of finite type, dominance over an
algebraically closed field implies surjectivity on all scheme points;
over any field, schematic dominance suffices. Over any field with reduced
target `H`, dominance or injectivity of the compatible coordinate map
`A → B` gives `Module.FaithfullyFlat A B` for its given algebra structure.
The coordinate presentations may have independent universes.
For finite-type commutative Hopf algebras over any field, an injective
morphism `f : A →ₐc[K] B` with reduced source coordinate algebra `A` satisfies
`f.toAlgHom.toRingHom.FaithfullyFlat`, by
[`BialgHom.faithfullyFlat_of_injective_of_isReduced`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/algebraic-groups/blob/cad2dc41da14fb003738f0a032601dfa4d203453/AlgebraicGroups/Algebra/HopfAlgebra/FaithfullyFlat/Reduced.lean).
This uses the given Hopf structures, in independent scalar and carrier universes.
See [surjectivity over algebraically closed fields](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/algebraic-groups/blob/cad2dc41da14fb003738f0a032601dfa4d203453/AlgebraicGroups/GroupScheme/Surjective.lean),
[schematic dominance over fields](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/algebraic-groups/blob/cad2dc41da14fb003738f0a032601dfa4d203453/AlgebraicGroups/GroupScheme/SurjectiveBaseChange.lean), and
[faithful flatness of coordinates](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/algebraic-groups/blob/cad2dc41da14fb003738f0a032601dfa4d203453/AlgebraicGroups/GroupScheme/FaithfullyFlatCoordinates.lean).

headlines.title: Hopf tensor–quotient equivalences
headlines.text:
For a central bialgebra map from a
commutative bialgebra `A` over a commutative ring `R` to a possibly
noncommutative Hopf algebra `B`, comultiplication gives a first-factor
`B`-linear equivalence `B ⊗[A] B ≃ₗ[B] B ⊗[R] (B / (ker ε_A)B)`.
In this generality the quotient is only a module quotient, and `A` need
not have an antipode. When `B` is commutative,
`HopfAlgebra.tensorQuotientAlgEquiv` refines the same map to a `B`-algebra
equivalence on the canonical tensor and quotient algebras. The simp equality
`tensorQuotientAlgEquiv_toLinearEquiv` recovers `tensorQuotientEquiv`, so its
finite-comultiplication formulas compute both directions. For a group-like
`c`, the inverse sends `(b c) ⊗ [c]` to `b ⊗ c`. Mixed scalar extension is
the composition of inverse tensor cancellation, congruence with this
refinement, and tensor cancellation. Compatible ordinary algebra maps
and scalar towers suffice; the commutative coefficient algebra needs no
Hopf structure.
See [`HopfAlgebra/TensorQuotient`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/algebraic-groups/blob/cad2dc41da14fb003738f0a032601dfa4d203453/AlgebraicGroups/Algebra/HopfAlgebra/TensorQuotient.lean).

headlines.title: Finite Hopf algebras and Hopf modules
headlines.text:
Every finite-dimensional Hopf
algebra over a field has a linear functional `λ` such that `λ (a * x)`
is nondegenerate in both arguments. Its left regular module is injective
(`HopfAlgebra.injective_self`). The algebra need not be commutative or
cocommutative, and the field may have any characteristic.
See [the Frobenius and self-injectivity theorems](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/algebraic-groups/blob/cad2dc41da14fb003738f0a032601dfa4d203453/AlgebraicGroups/Algebra/HopfAlgebra/Frobenius.lean).
For decomposition over a commutative semiring `R`, let
`H` be a possibly noncommutative semiring with full Hopf algebra structure, and
`X` a specified right comodule on an additive-commutative-monoid `R`-module `M`.
For its given right action with `IsScalarTower R Hᵐᵒᵖ M`, an explicit
`hX : X.IsHopfModule` gives
`X.coinvariantsTensorEquiv hX : (X.weightSpace (1 : H)) ⊗[R] H ≃ₗ[R] M`.
The forward map is the given action. The inverse `X.toCoinvariantsTensor hX`
corestricts the antipode contraction to coinvariants before tensoring it with
`H` and composing with the coaction. Both inverse identities hold, including
the tensor-side identity inside coinvariants tensored with `H` itself. Both
maps intertwine the given right action with right multiplication on the `H`
factor. Universes are independent; no flatness, finiteness or inverse antipode
is required.
See [the decomposition and its API](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/algebraic-groups/blob/cad2dc41da14fb003738f0a032601dfa4d203453/AlgebraicGroups/Algebra/Coalgebra/RightComodule/HopfModule/Decomposition.lean).
